svg.text: RFC006: Uncertainty Quantification Framework for vEcoli Whole-Cell Simulations

text.tspan: Implement UQ framework to track prediction confidence

svg.text: Deconvolves generation, lineage seed, and cell cycle variance to model bulk vs. single-cell relationships (RFC006 §1)
Temporal aggregation of subsampled trajectories (RFC006 §4, Step B)
“Across all cells, all times — which parameters drive output variance?”
Elementary Effect for parameter i at point x:
• σ = std(EE_i) — high → nonlinear or interactive
Cost: O(r × (n+1)) evaluations vs O(n²) for Sobol MC
n params → K params (K ≪ n) for efficient PCE fitting
• c_α fit via least-squares on LHS samples (N points)
Or: load precomputed (X, Y) from cache (Stage 2 mode)
STEP 7a: Sobol Indices from PCE Coefficients
Variance-based sensitivity from the PCE expansion (no additional sampling):
S_i = Var_i[E(Y|X_i)] / Var(Y) = ∑{α:α_i>0, α_j=0∀j≠i} c_α² / ∑{α≠0} c_α²
• S_i = first-order (main effect) — fraction of Var(Y) from x_i alone
• S_Ti = total-order — includes all interactions involving x_i (S_Ti ≥ S_i, gap = interactions)
Example: “vio_expression drives 60% of bulk mass variance, mecillinam_conc drives 25%”
“Within each cell cycle stage — which parameters matter?”
Per RFC006 §3: “The choice of the cell cycle variable
will be informed by the sensitivity analyses (1-3)”
Rank observables by residual variance fraction.
High residual → variance NOT from gen/seed → likely cell-cycle-driven
STEP 6b: Koopman DMD → Cell Cycle Variable θ
Dynamic Mode Decomposition on selected observables:
Per RFC006: “deterministic function with cyclic behaviour”
STEP 6c/6d: Strategy 4 — Cell Cycle Stratification (RFC006 §1, Strategy 4)
Bin timepoints into n_bins stages by θ (default 10, uniform partitions of [0,1]):
Stage k: θ ∈ [k/n_bins, (k+1)/n_bins) → Ȳ_k = mean(Y | θ ∈ stage k)
• θ ≈ 0.0–0.15: B-period (birth → replication init) • θ ≈ 0.2–0.7: C-period (DNA replication)
• θ ≈ 0.7–1.0: D-period (post-replication → division) • Mass doubles: ~1.03 → 1.91 across cycle
Strategy4Wrapper: f_stage4(x) = bin(θ(f(x))) → per-stage means as objective function for PCE
For each cell cycle stage k, fit independent PCE and compute Sobol:
S_i^(k) = Var_i[E(Ȳ_k | X_i)] / Var(Ȳ_k) for k = 0, ..., n_bins−1
Phase 2 Sobol are NOT time-averages of Phase 1 — they are orthogonal decompositions
(like “between countries” vs “within countries” for total variance of human height)
Example: “During C-period, mecillinam_conc drives 80% of variance; during D-period, vio_expression dominates”
(Phase 1 variance decomposition informs Phase 2 observable selection — RFC006 §3)
→ Step 5b: rank by residual, select top-K
→ Step 6b: Koopman DMD on selected obs
├ SobolIndices (1 set) — S_i, S_Ti per parameter across all cells
├ PCESurrogate — cheap polynomial approximation of f(x)
├ variance_decomposition — gen_frac, seed_frac, residual per observable
├ list[SobolIndices] (n_bins sets) — S_i^(k), S_Ti^(k) per cell cycle stage
├ CellCycleRelevanceResult — which observables track the cell cycle
├ cell_cycle_profile — per-stage mass/growth means across θ-bins
└ Koopman spectrum — eigenvalues, frequencies, mode shapes
Phase 1 and Phase 2 are orthogonal decompositions of the same total variance. Phase 1 collapses time; Phase 2 conditions on cell cycle stage.
Key Concepts — Mathematical and Biological Reference
Quantifies how input parameter uncertainty propagates to output variance.
S_i = V_i / Var(Y) — main effect of parameter i
S_Ti = 1 − Var(E[Y|X_~i]) / Var(Y) — total effect including all interactions
PCE avoids brute-force Monte Carlo: Sobol indices are computed analytically
from the PCE coefficient matrix — no additional sampling required.
Approximate stochastic model response by orthogonal polynomial expansion.
For uniform inputs on [a,b]: use Legendre polynomials P_n(x).
Coefficients fitted via least-squares regression on Latin Hypercube Samples.
Result: a fast-evaluating surrogate f̂(x) ≈ f(x) with R² goodness-of-fit.
B period (θ ≈ 0.0–0.15): Birth to replication initiation. Duration varies with growth rate.
C period (θ ≈ 0.2–0.7): Active DNA replication (oriC → terC), ~40 min, relatively constant.
D period (θ ≈ 0.7–1.0): Post-replication to division, ~20 min. Septation and cell division.
Mass approximately doubles per cycle. Growth rate dips during D-period (septation).
θ ∈ [0,1] is a continuous coordinate, not the 3 discrete phases — 10 bins
give enough resolution for polynomial fitting while keeping bins well-populated.
DMD approximates the Koopman operator K: g(x_{t+1}) = K g(x_t)
Identifies oscillatory modes as eigenvalues λ = |λ|e^(iω) on the unit circle.
The mode nearest ω ≈ 2π/T_cycle is the cell cycle mode.
Its eigenfunction phase provides a data-driven, assumption-free cell cycle
coordinate. Robust to noise and individual cell variation.
RFC006 — Roadmap for uncertainty quantification framework | Milestone 08.4.2 | Key modules: pipe.py, sensitivity.py, cell_cycle.py, koopman.py, pce/surrogate.py
